frontmatter.number: The ordinal within this subject directory.
frontmatter.subject: What is modeled, as one noun phrase.
frontmatter.status: One of: draft, settled, superseded by N.

scope.models: What this model names, at the conceptual level.
scope.abstraction: The statement that this model is independent of implementation, protocol, and encoding, and that no detail of any of the three appears in a normative section.

excludes.subject: A thing this model does not name.

primitives.term: A term taken as undefined by this model.
primitives.assumed: What this model assumes about it, exhaustively.

category.name: The category name.
category.recognition-rule: What places a candidate in this category.

boundary-example.inside: A candidate near the line that falls in this category.
boundary-example.outside: The nearest candidate that falls in another, and which.

categories.exhaustive: Whether every candidate falls in exactly one category. If not, what falls in none, and what that means.

term.name: A term the procedure turns on.
term.definition: Its definition at the level the procedure uses it.

criterion.procedure: One ordered cascade. First match decides. Two readers applying it to one candidate reach one result.

step.test: The question asked at this step.
step.outcome: The category or disposition assigned when it matches.

criterion.terminal-outcome: The disposition of a candidate that matches no step.

objects.declaration-order: Whether declaration order is significant, and what changing it breaks.

object.name: The object name.
object.category: The category from the categories section.

property.name: The property name.
property.value-space: What values this property admits, exhaustively, with its equivalence: which distinct spellings denote one value, or the statement that it has no notation and so no second spelling.
property.stated-over: The statement that this property is stated over the object itself. No property is stated over an encoding, a representation, or a storage form.

object.formation-rule: The rule under which a candidate is concluded to be this object, stated as premises and a conclusion.
object.refuses: What this object cannot hold or cannot assert.
object.irreducible: Why the remaining objects cannot express this one. Marked non-normative. May name other objects.
object.absence: The concrete operation that becomes impossible without this object. An operation, not a principle.

relationship.name: The relationship name.

participant.cardinality: How many instances occupy this position.

relationship.direction: Whether the relationship is directed, and from which position.
relationship.constraint: A condition that must hold between the participants.
relationship.absence: The concrete operation that becomes impossible without this relationship.

relationships.closed: Whether the set of relationships is closed, and under what criterion.

judgment.name: The judgment name.
judgment.form: The judgment form, with its metavariables named.
judgment.conclusion: The conclusion drawn when the premises hold.

composition.well-formed: Which structures over the objects and relationships are well-formed.
composition.underivable: Which structures have no derivation, stated so that the absence of a derivation is checkable.
composition.dynamics: The statement of whether this model defines evaluation, reduction, or any operation other than formation, and which.

refusal.lost: The capability that is gone as a result.

subsumption.candidate: The candidate not admitted as its own object.
subsumption.carrier: The object or composition that carries its case.
subsumption.expression: How the case is expressed using the carrier.

invariant.claim: What holds over the whole model.
invariant.refuter: The observation, made by reading this document alone, that shows the claim false. A refuter naming an artifact this document does not state is not permitted.

boundary.realization-class: The class of realization this boundary binds. State whether one realization or many derive from this model.

must-supply.owner: The single owner of this obligation.

boundary.may-choose: A decision a realization makes freely, stated as a freedom.
boundary.may-not-decide: A decision reserved to this model or to a named other model.
boundary.direction: The statement that every obligation runs from this model to a realization, and that no claim in a normative section above depends on a realization's choice.

decision.decision-made: The decision, as stated in a normative section above.
decision.failure-prevented: The concrete failure the decision prevents.

item.fact: A fact settled here that another document must carry.
item.owner: The single document that carries it.
